title: Mrs. Vivien Hidary: "Parashat Mishpatim"

chapters.title: Introduction to Parashat Mishpatim
chapters.about: Resilience, Har Sinai, and the transition from the revelation to the laws.

chapters.title: The Mountain and the People's Reaction
chapters.about: The experience at Har Sinai and the people's fear of the divine.

chapters.title: Building a Foundation for Connection
chapters.about: The three relationships: man to man, man to God, and man to self.

chapters.title: Overcoming the Slave Mentality
chapters.about: Moving beyond victimhood and the obligation to rise above past suffering.

chapters.title: Shalom and Making Things Whole
chapters.about: The concept of shalem and finding peace through responsibility.

chapters.title: Meat, Dairy, and Kindness
chapters.about: Using the law of meat and dairy as a metaphor for approaching others with kindness.

chapters.title: Angels and Divine Protection
chapters.about: The presence of angels and the blessing of Yaakov Abinu.

chapters.title: The Donkey and Physicality
chapters.about: The law of the burdened donkey and its connection to the physical world.

summary: Mrs. Hidary explores the spiritual significance of Parashat Mishpatim, framing the laws as a guide for building healthy relationships with oneself, others, and Hashem. She discusses how to overcome a victim mentality and explains how the laws of the Torah serve as a practical foundation for personal growth and connection. The class also touches on the deeper meanings behind specific laws, such as the prohibition against cooking a goat in its mother's milk and the obligation to help a burdened animal.
questions: Why are the laws of Parashat Mishpatim given immediately after the revelation at Har Sinai?
How can we move past a victim mentality to build a stronger relationship with Hashem?
What is the deeper, personal meaning behind the law of not cooking a goat in its mother's milk?
How does the law of helping a burdened animal apply to our modern lives and humanitarian efforts?
Why does the Torah emphasize that we are not alone in our journey?
